composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Gusto, so create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio has no managed Gusto app, and Gusto only issues production keys to approved partners, so you must register your own application and use its credentials in a Composio auth config.

scenarios.label: Public agent integration for Gusto customers
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your AI agent connects Gusto accounts of customers outside your company in production.

prerequisites.title: Security audit evidence and contacts
prerequisites.detail: Prepare audit reports (e.g. SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS), penetration test reports and security/incident policies, or a list of controls if you have no audit. Name a security contact and an incident response contact.

prerequisites.title: Partner status with Gusto
prerequisites.detail: The API is restricted to Gusto App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners.

steps.title: Build and test in sandbox
steps.detail: Get sandbox keys from the Developer Portal and test your integration in the demo environment.
steps.done_when: Your use case works end to end in the demo environment.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom Gusto auth config through Composio's API using your client ID and secret, with the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists in Composio and a sandbox connection succeeds.

steps.title: Draft Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: Draft the use-case description and requested scopes for the application.
steps.done_when: Draft is ready for your review.

steps.title: Submit pre-approval application
steps.detail: Submit the application with company and business details.

steps.title: Wait for Partnerships review
steps.detail: No action is needed until Gusto replies. Duration is not documented.

steps.title: Complete Security Review
steps.detail: Provide audit or control information, penetration test reports, policies and contacts.
steps.done_when: GRC team accepts the Security Review.

steps.title: Pass QA review and get keys
steps.detail: Gusto reviews build quality before issuing production keys.

steps.title: Swap in production credentials
steps.detail: Update the Composio auth config with production client ID and secret and test with an admin.
steps.done_when: A customer admin can authorize and the agent can call allowed scopes.

traps.title: Scopes are fixed by Gusto
traps.detail: Calls outside your assigned scopes are rejected in production, and extra scopes must be requested after release.

traps.title: No demo accounts in production
traps.detail: Demo or test accounts are not supported in production, so all pre-approval testing stays in sandbox.

traps.title: Gates run in sequence
traps.detail: The Security Review starts only after pre-approval is granted, so delays add up.

blockers.what_it_means: Gusto has not approved pre-approval, security review and QA, or has not accepted you as a partner.
blockers.what_to_do: Complete each gate in order and contact Gusto's partnerships team if stalled.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the application and security documentation for review.

blockers.what_it_means: Only primary or full-access admins can enable a new application's access.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's primary or full-access admin to complete the OAuth step.

evidence.answer: This page is general white-labeling guidance, not Gusto-specific. Proxying the redirect through your own domain is optional and is only for hiding Composio's domain.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: When proxying, you set the authorized redirect URI in your OAuth app's settings to your own endpoint.

evidence.answer: The example redirect URI for the proxy is on your own domain, using https.

evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect and must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.

evidence.answer: Without your own OAuth app, the provider consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' on services such as Google and GitHub.

evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through Composio's backend domain so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.answer: Composio's OAuth callback URL, which the proxy forwards to, is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits also display Composio's backend URL on the consent screen.

evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains its own OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so the developer does not need to register one.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for polling triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With managed apps, users see a consent screen saying Composio wants to access their account, instead of the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not include everything a developer needs, such as write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a toolkit, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
evidence.answer: A custom auth config can be created for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances even when a managed app exists.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest.
evidence.answer: A developer may mix approaches: own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (the page names GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest, with each toolkit having its own auth config.
